claim_set.claim_text: Every AI-generated financial entry, statement, or filing that moves toward a consequential action MUST map to a recorded named-authority decision — the agent, the entry / statement / filing artefact, the intended consequential action, and the named accountant / director under whose authority it proceeds. Entries lacking a recorded authority decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Before an AI-generated entry proceeds to a consequential action it MUST carry a recorded due-diligence result — competence, recognition-and-measurement / true-and-fair basis, and an accounting-records-adequacy / fraud-risk screen (Companies Act 2006 s.386; ISA (UK) 240 / 315) where applicable. An unscreened, low-confidence, or records-deficient entry is refused.

Every AI-generated entry that proceeds toward a consequential action MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin binding the generating model and version, the inputs and pinned source data, the recognition / measurement basis applied, the due-diligence result relied on, and the named-authority outcome — audit-grade, SOX §404-aligned data-integrity provenance verifiable offline, satisfying Companies Act 2006 s.386 records adequacy and UK MTD digital record-keeping.

An AI-generated entry MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT drive a consequential action until a named human reviewer — the accountant-of-record, the engagement partner, or a responsible finance director — records sign-off. The irreversible Companies House statutory filing additionally requires §36 two-person sign-off (the preparing accountant AND an approving director). Unreviewed AI-driven consequential actions are refused and routed dual-channel.

KYE governs WHETHER an AI-generated financial entry/statement/filing may proceed to a consequential action and PROVES the basis. KYE does not compute the numbers, prepare the accounts, run the accounting engine, or judge whether the accounts are correct.
